consequence.statement: Operators upgrading to Crossplane 2.0 must configure managed resource activation policies as step 3 of the documented upgrade approach; the cited excerpt names the step but does not state what fails if it is skipped.
consequence.remediation: Follow section 3, "Configure managed resource activation policies", of the Crossplane v2 upgrade guide (upgrade-to-crossplane-v2.md) when upgrading to 2.0.0.

original.statement: Upgrading to Crossplane 2.0 includes an operator step to configure managed resource activation policies, listed as step 3 of the upgrade approach in the official v2 upgrade guide.

consequence.statement: If the operator does nothing, the default MRAP that Crossplane v2 creates automatically activates all managed resources (`*`). The upgrade guide describes replacing it with a targeted MRAP as optional, for better cluster resource efficiency. Nothing is stated to fail.
consequence.remediation: Optional: before installing v2 providers, check which managed resources you use and replace the default MRAP with a targeted one that activates only those resources (step 3 of the Crossplane v2 upgrade guide).

corrected.statement: Crossplane 2.0 automatically creates a default managed resource activation policy (MRAP) that activates all managed resources (`*`). Customizing it before installing v2 providers is optional, so an operator who does nothing has no operational consequence.

decision.reason: The section context [ev-06a16cdbc869] says Crossplane v2 automatically creates a default MRAP that activates all managed resources (`*`), and that operators can "optionally" customize it for better cluster resource efficiency. So an operator who does nothing still has every managed resource activated, and nothing fails or needs migrating. [ev-188e63ccea10] only names the step. migration-required overstates this, so the consequence is none (informational), with optional tuning as the remediation.
